newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds turn around to end up on U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds turn around to end up on U.S. mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Thursday, closely following the early fall and subsequent rise of U.S. Treasuries.

Argentine bonds tracked the U.S. market lower early and then rose with it late after a well received 30-year bond auction in the United States. Traders predicted the market would be range-bound in coming days, on account of U.S. holidays on Monday and subdued demand from institutional investors.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/8 to 83-1/2, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 119.60.
